topic: Captive portal testing setup and next steps
summary_markdown:
The team discussed data inconsistencies found during captive portal testing. To standardize the experiment, it was decided to run a 'clean experiment' using a single frequency band and a single channel.

Technical setup adjustments were made: RUT, TPLink, and x11 devices were configured to listen on Channel 1. It was noted that raw data contains a `freq` field which can identify the active channel.

A separate test idea was raised for RZK terminals: using one terminal and switching all Access Points (APs) and the RUT200 to the same channel for a week, while maintaining 5GHz operation.

Preliminary findings highlighted differences in device broadcasting behavior across channels (e.g., Samsung/iPhone broadcast on all channels; Huawei broadcasts on the connected channel). Furthermore, it was observed that event tracking fails when the 5GHz interface is disabled on the APs.
decisions: The team will run a 'clean experiment' using one frequency band and one channel to eliminate data variance.
RUT, TPLink, and x11 devices were configured to operate on Channel 1 for testing.
A separate test was planned for RZK terminals: setting all APs and the RUT200 to a single channel for one terminal.
action_items: Someone needs to check why captive events cannot be seen when the 5GHz interface is disabled on the AP.
